# CLI reference

## `openshell-annotate`

```text
Policy-as-code for OpenShell: scan @openshell source directives and generate/validate policy.yaml

Usage: openshell-annotate [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  scan       List directives with file:line
  generate   Generate policy.yaml (and a providers file) from directives
  lint       Validate directives, find un-annotated network/fs/secret call sites, optionally check a policy file
  diff-logs  Map sandbox allow/deny events (OCSF JSON lines or `openshell logs` shorthand) back to directives: suggest missing ones, flag stale ones. Exit 1 when directives are missing
  docs       Generate the reference docs (CLI.md, DIRECTIVES.md) from the code; `--check` fails if the committed ones are stale
  drift      Compare the policy generated from directives with a committed policy.yaml (CI gate)
  help       Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --root <ROOT>
          Repository root: paths in output are relative to it; `openshell-annotate.toml` is read from it

          [default: .]

      --config <CONFIG>
          Config file (default: <root>/openshell-annotate.toml if present)

  -h, --help
          Print help

  -V, --version
          Print version
```

## `openshell-annotate scan`

```text
List directives with file:line

Usage: openshell-annotate scan [OPTIONS] [PATHS]...

Arguments:
  [PATHS]...
          Files or directories to process (default: the whole root)

Options:
      --json
          Alias for `--format json`

      --format <FORMAT>
          Output format

          Possible values:
          - human:   Multi-line report with source context, icons and colour (the default)
          - json:    Machine-readable JSON (stable). For `generate` the policy stays on stdout and the JSON summary goes to stderr
          - compact: One line per item, the plain output of earlier versions (stable; for scripts and CI logs)

          [default: human]

      --color <COLOR>
          Colour for the human format

          Possible values:
          - auto:   Colour when the output stream is a terminal (stdout; stderr for the `generate` summary); honours NO_COLOR, CLICOLOR_FORCE and TERM=dumb
          - always
          - never

          [default: auto]

      --no-icons
          Plain ASCII in the human format (no emoji or Unicode icons). Icons also turn off by themselves when the locale is not UTF-8 or TERM=dumb

          [alias: --ascii]

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## `openshell-annotate generate`

```text
Generate policy.yaml (and a providers file) from directives.

The policy YAML is the only thing on stdout (or in --output) whatever the format, so piping is safe. The summary (rules, files, sources, warnings) goes to stderr and follows --format, --color and --no-icons.

Usage: openshell-annotate generate [OPTIONS] [PATHS]...

Arguments:
  [PATHS]...
          Files or directories to process (default: the whole root)

Options:
  -o, --output <OUTPUT>
          Write policy here (default: stdout)

      --providers-out <PROVIDERS_OUT>
          Write providers here: `.sh` = setup script, anything else = JSON

      --profiles-dir <PROFILES_DIR>
          Provider-profile directory (overrides [providers].profiles_dir)

      --format <FORMAT>
          Output format

          Possible values:
          - human:   Multi-line report with source context, icons and colour (the default)
          - json:    Machine-readable JSON (stable). For `generate` the policy stays on stdout and the JSON summary goes to stderr
          - compact: One line per item, the plain output of earlier versions (stable; for scripts and CI logs)

          [default: human]

      --color <COLOR>
          Colour for the human format

          Possible values:
          - auto:   Colour when the output stream is a terminal (stdout; stderr for the `generate` summary); honours NO_COLOR, CLICOLOR_FORCE and TERM=dumb
          - always
          - never

          [default: auto]

      --no-icons
          Plain ASCII in the human format (no emoji or Unicode icons). Icons also turn off by themselves when the locale is not UTF-8 or TERM=dumb

          [alias: --ascii]

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## `openshell-annotate diff-logs`

```text
Map sandbox allow/deny events (OCSF JSON lines or `openshell logs` shorthand) back to directives: suggest missing ones, flag stale ones. Exit 1 when directives are missing

Usage: openshell-annotate diff-logs [OPTIONS] [LOGS]...

Arguments:
  [LOGS]...
          Log files (`-` = stdin). OCSF JSONL (`/var/log/openshell-ocsf.*.jsonl`) and `openshell logs` output both work

Options:
      --write
          Apply the suggested directives to the sources (or to --observed-file when no source mentions the host)

      --observed-file <OBSERVED_FILE>
          File that receives suggestions no source line mentions (relative to --root)

          [default: openshell/observed-egress.sh]

      --deny-stale
          Also exit 1 when stale directives are found

      --json
          Alias for `--format json`

      --format <FORMAT>
          Output format

          Possible values:
          - human:   Multi-line report with source context, icons and colour (the default)
          - json:    Machine-readable JSON (stable). For `generate` the policy stays on stdout and the JSON summary goes to stderr
          - compact: One line per item, the plain output of earlier versions (stable; for scripts and CI logs)

          [default: human]

      --color <COLOR>
          Colour for the human format

          Possible values:
          - auto:   Colour when the output stream is a terminal (stdout; stderr for the `generate` summary); honours NO_COLOR, CLICOLOR_FORCE and TERM=dumb
          - always
          - never

          [default: auto]

      --no-icons
          Plain ASCII in the human format (no emoji or Unicode icons). Icons also turn off by themselves when the locale is not UTF-8 or TERM=dumb

          [alias: --ascii]

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## `openshell-annotate docs`

```text
Generate the reference docs (CLI.md, DIRECTIVES.md) from the code; `--check` fails if the committed ones are stale

Usage: openshell-annotate docs [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --out <OUT>
          Output directory

          [default: docs]

      --check
          Do not write; exit 1 when the files in --out differ from what the code generates

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `openshell-annotate drift`

```text
Compare the policy generated from directives with a committed policy.yaml (CI gate)

Usage: openshell-annotate drift [OPTIONS] --policy <POLICY> [PATHS]...

Arguments:
  [PATHS]...
          Files or directories to process (default: the whole root)

Options:
      --policy <POLICY>


      --providers <PROVIDERS>
          Also compare a committed providers JSON file

      --profiles-dir <PROFILES_DIR>


      --strict
          Flag committed sections directives cannot express (landlock, network_middlewares)

      --json


  -h, --help
          Print help
```
